# Results — Study 857 (SG&A Cost Stickiness)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **sticky-cost
firms under-earn**: a firm whose SG&A stays sticky into a sales decline (Anderson-Banker-
Janakiraman β₂ ≪ 0) is running weaker operating discipline and should deliver lower forward
returns. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every
number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the partial current month is
dropped). Prices Fingerprint `2cf202cb4854` (yfinance daily adjusted closes); events cache = 314
(ticker, filing) rows.*

*Data stamp: as-of 2026-06-30 · Fingerprint `2cf202cb4854` · 314 events · 25 identified names.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Universe | **33** large US filers reporting `SellingGeneralAndAdministrativeExpense` on EDGAR; **25** identify a point-in-time stickiness estimate (fixed, current survivors) |
| Signal source | SEC EDGAR XBRL `companyconcept`: `SellingGeneralAndAdministrativeExpense` + `Revenues`/`RevenueFromContractWithCustomer…` (quarterly), `NetIncomeLoss` + `Assets` (profitability axis); de-duplicated on period end, earliest filing kept |
| Panel | **314** point-in-time stickiness quarters, period ends **2015-09-26 → 2026-05-03**, stamped with the **10-Q/10-K filing date** (expanding-window estimate; no look-ahead) |
| Prices | yfinance daily adjusted (total-return) closes, sliced to 2026-06-30 |
| Estimator | ABJ `Δlog(SG&A)=β₀+β₁·Δlog(Sales)+β₂·(Decrease·Δlog(Sales))` on an expanding window of only public YoY obs; `stickiness = −β₂`; trade signal `disc = β₂` (higher ⇒ leaner). Guards: ≥20 obs, ≥4 decline quarters |
| Primary test | calendar-time monthly long-short: rank fresh `disc` into **terciles**, long leanest / short stickiest, earn **next** month's return (one execution lag); decisive stat = **Newey-West (6-lag) t** |
| Costs | one-way × NAV × monthly turnover on both legs + annualised borrow on the short leg |

**Coverage caveat (first-class).** Only **25 of 33** names ever identify β₂ — steady growers
(WMT, COST, HD, NKE, AAPL, PFE…) rarely post a YoY sales *decline*, so the estimable panel is
**cyclical-tilted** (semis, industrials, hardware, materials). The expanding-window estimate
only matures ~4-5 years into each name's XBRL history, so the signal starts **2015** and the
monthly cross-section is small (avg **11 names**). Firm-level β₂ from noisy quarterly windows is
dispersed (final per-firm stickiness ranges −1.06 to +3.04); **12 of 25** names estimate as
sticky. Terciles on a thin, noisy cross-section are noisy by construction. No survivorship
correction: current survivors — named on the Signal axis (and the bias runs *against* the
claim; see docs/references.md).

## The phenomenon is real — SG&A **is** sticky in aggregate (ABJ replicates)

Pooled across all 314 firm-quarter estimates, the average asymmetry:

| quantity | value | reading |
|---|--:|---|
| mean β₁ (response to a sales **increase**) | **+0.651** | SG&A rises 0.65% per 1% sales gain |
| mean β₁+β₂ (response to a sales **decrease**) | **+0.554** | it falls only 0.55% per 1% sales loss |
| mean β₂ (the asymmetry) | **−0.097** | costs cling on the way down — **stickiness confirmed** |

The Anderson-Banker-Janakiraman effect **replicates** (β₁ > β₁+β₂: costs are sticky), milder
than ABJ's original 0.55 / 0.35 because we estimate at quarterly YoY frequency. So the input
phenomenon is genuine. The question is whether the *cross-sectional* stickiness estimate earns
anything — and there the answer is no.

## Headline — the forward-return long-short (do sticky firms under-earn?)

Monthly rebalanced tercile long-short on `disc` (long leanest / short stickiest), one execution
lag, 2015-12 → 2026-06 (**101 months**, avg cross-section 11.0 names):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| long-short mean | **−28.6 bps/month** (−3.43%/yr, gross) |
| one-sample *t* | −0.57 |
| **Newey-West (6-lag) *t*** | **−0.45** |
| Sharpe (gross, ann.) | −0.20 |
| monthly hit rate | 48% |
| long (lean) leg / short (sticky) leg | +125.2 / +153.7 bps/month |
| growth of \$1 (gross) | ×0.66 over 101 months |

The claim predicts a **positive** spread (lean firms out-earn). The point estimate is the wrong
sign and insignificant (**NW *t* = −0.45**), and it is **not even sign-stable**: a staleness-120
variant flips to **+28.1 bps, NW *t* = +0.66**. Either way the effect is statistically zero.
Note the sticky (short) leg *out-returned* the lean (long) leg on average here — the opposite of
the thesis — but by nothing you could distinguish from noise.

## Cross-check — pooled event drift (tercile sort by `disc`)

Bucket all (ticker, filing) events by `disc`; top-minus-bottom forward drift, entered one day
after the filing:

| horizon | n | top (lean) | bottom (sticky) | long-short | one-sample *t* | win | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 21 d (≈1 m) | 313 | +1.37% | +1.72% | **−0.35%** | −0.32 | 50% | 0.62 |
| 63 d (≈1 q) | 301 | +5.92% | +4.65% | **+1.27%** | +0.57 | 54% | 0.25 |
| 126 d (≈2 q) | 296 | +10.77% | +11.52% | **−0.76%** | −0.24 | 54% | 0.59 |

Flat and **sign-inconsistent across horizons** (−0.35% / +1.27% / −0.76%). The 63-day tercile
means are mildly monotone (+4.65% / +4.85% / +5.92% low→high, the only horizon that leans the
claim's way), but the long-short *t* never exceeds +0.57 and the label-shuffle placebo *p* sits
at 0.25-0.62 — a random tercile split routinely beats the real one. There is **no forward-return
sort** in this signal on this tape.

## Era split — no regime rescues it (and the sign flips)

Calendar long-short, split at 2020-07-01 (the COVID sales shock):

| era | months | mean | Newey-West *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| pre-2020H2 | 54 | +14.4 bps | +0.20 |
| 2020H2-2026 | 47 | −78.0 bps | −0.74 |

The two halves carry **opposite-signed** insignificant means. This is the signature of noise,
not a decayed edge.

## Third axis — does stickiness predict weaker future **profitability**?

Pooled OLS of the change in trailing-four-quarter ROA over the next ~year on the stickiness
measure (n = 226 matched events):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| slope *b* | **+0.0004** |
| *t* (iid-pooled) | +0.15 |
| R² | 0.000 |
| Pearson correlation | **+0.010** |
| next-year ROA change, top stickiness tercile | +0.34 pp |
| next-year ROA change, bottom stickiness tercile | +0.48 pp |
| tercile spread (top − bottom) | **−0.14 pp** |

Essentially **zero**. The tercile spread is *directionally* consistent with the claim (the
stickiest third sees ROA improve 0.14 pp *less*) but the magnitude is trivial and the
correlation is +0.01 — within noise of nothing. Cost stickiness, as estimated point-in-time from
these thin quarterly windows, **does not forecast weaker operating results** either. (Attenuation
from a noisy firm-level β₂ is a real caveat — but the returns null does not hinge on it.)

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic SG&A + sales *levels* obeying a per-firm true β₂, run through the **same**
estimator, with a TUNABLE planted forward-return link (lean names drift up); no network.
Detector = the primary calendar long-short NW *t*.

| world | Newey-West *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (edge = 0), **10 seeds** | mean **+0.02** (sd 0.87), \|t\| ≥ 2 in **0/10** seeds |
| planted edge = 0.35 (seed 857) | **+3.16** (mean +156.9 bps/month) |

The detector averages ≈0 on the null (0/10 HAC crossings) and lights up hard on a planted link.
The real-tape NW *t* = −0.45 is therefore a genuine null, not a broken pipeline. *(A faithful-
engine / power check only — never cited in support of a real-tape stamp.)*

## Tradability — the timer

Calendar long-short net of one-way costs × turnover (both legs) + short-leg borrow (monthly
turnover ≈ 0.07 — a very slow characteristic):

| cost (one-way) | borrow (ann.) | net mean | ~ann. | Newey-West *t* | Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 10 bps | 50 bps | −34.1 bps/mo | −4.10%/yr | −0.54 | −0.23 |
| 20 bps | 100 bps | −39.7 bps/mo | −4.77%/yr | −0.63 | −0.27 |

The gross spread is already the wrong sign and insignificant; costs only make a loss deeper.
There is nothing to trade.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The forward-return long-short is **wrong-signed and insignificant**
  (primary NW *t* = −0.45, one-sample −0.57), **sign-unstable** (staleness-120 flips to +0.66),
  the pooled event drift is **flat and sign-inconsistent** across horizons (long-short *t*
  ∈ [−0.32, +0.57], placebo *p* ≈ 0.25-0.62), and the two eras carry opposite-signed
  insignificant means. No robust |t| ≥ 2 in either direction on the real tape. The desk's
  definition of `NONE`.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The spread is not certifiable even gross (and is the wrong sign);
  net of realistic long-short costs + borrow it is −0.54 to −0.63 *t*, Sharpe ≈ −0.2. No
  paycheck.
- **"Is SG&A actually sticky?" — CONFIRMED (context axis).** The ABJ asymmetry **replicates** in
  aggregate (β₁ = +0.65 vs β₁+β₂ = +0.55; mean β₂ = −0.097). The *phenomenon* is real; it simply
  does not sort the cross-section of returns or forecast weaker future ROA (spread −0.14 pp,
  corr +0.01). A genuine accounting regularity that carries **no alpha and no clean profitability
  signal** on this panel.
